title: Desktop Automation MCP confirmation token
description: Single-use, short-lived confirmation token for guarded actions (text, close, drag). Runtime enforcement is implemented by the MCP server. NOTE: expires_at must be after issued_at (the lifetime cannot be negative/zero) and cannot be a past date; these cross-field and expiry checks cannot be expressed in JSON Schema, so they are performed by tools/validate_confirmation_token.py.

token_id.description: Unique identity of the token, in UUID4 form.

target_identity.description: Target identity the confirmation is bound to; same meaning as the current TargetSnapshot triple (hwnd/pid/process-start-time). Invalid on any other target or on second use.

hwnd.description: Window handle of the target top-level window.

pid.description: Process ID of the process owning the target window.

process_started_at.description: Process start time (FILETIME-like); same meaning as the current TargetSnapshot.process_started_at. Guards against PID reuse.

issued_at.description: Moment the token was issued; ISO-8601 date-time with MANDATORY numeric UTC offset (same rule as the expires_at constraint in schema/policy.schema.json). Bare 'Z' or offset-less values are not accepted.

expires_at.description: Moment the token expires; subject to the same offset rule as issued_at. NOTE: expires_at must be after issued_at and must not be a past date; tools/validate_confirmation_token.py rejects violations.

single_use.description: Design decision: in this first version every token is single-use, no multi-use.

consumed_at.description: Optional; filled when the token is consumed (a past date is normal since it is a consumption record, expiry rejection does not apply; but it cannot be before issued_at).
